name: team_add
unavailable: The person allows one agent in this chat: there is no team. Do the work yourself.
description:
Add a member to your team and start it at once, in the background, on its part of the work. You lead: members do the work while you plan, coordinate and review — once you have a member, tools that change things are refused to you.

- `name` is how everyone addresses it: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, after what it owns (`parser`, `api-tests`), unique in the team.
- `role` is one line: what it owns. `task` is its brief and must stand on its own — it sees nothing of this conversation: what to do, when it is done, and what to report.
- `goal` is the team's goal in a line; your first member needs it, and every member is told it.
- `lead: true` lets it add members of its own and lead an area; it then manages as you do.
- The person sets how many agents the team may have; past that this is refused. When the model is already serving as many requests as it can at once, the member waits for a slot and starts when one frees.
- Its final reply comes to you as its report. Meanwhile team_send messages it, team_read shows the team and the room, team_stop stops it.
- Agents: {{agents}}

name.description: Its name in the team, after what it owns

goal.description: The team's goal in one line: needed with your first member; a new one is told to members added from now on

lead.description: May add members of its own and lead an area (default: false)

model.description: Run it on another model — only one the person named in this conversation (its id or name, as in the list in your instructions). Default: the session's model.

variables.agents: the agents a member may be: `name — description`, separated by "; " (as task's)
